column1: # clipfmt rules: what a copied link pastes as in apps that read rich text, like Slack.
# id <TAB> pattern (the whole link) <TAB> format <TAB> an example link <TAB> what the example pastes as
# in a format, {1} {2}... are the pattern's groups (URL-decoded), {1:words} the same with its
# - _ or + as spaces, and {host} the link's host. $ and \ are as typed. an id can have more
# than one line, with one format.
# every rule is off until you turn it on in dott clipfmt, which can also add a rule from an
# example link. rules for this Mac only go in ~/.config/clipfmt/local.tsv (same columns); a
# line there hides this file's lines with its id. clipfmt reloads both by itself.
#   bash ~/dotfiles/clipfmt/clipfmt.sh test   checks each example pastes as its last column
# your rules for every machine (dott clipfmt, add a link rule, adds them here)
